title: Jonah and the Wolf
premise: Lior Hartwell, a runaway apprentice hiding in the Ledgerhouse of the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers that every entry she keeps is a thread in an ancient covenant binding the human realm to the wolf-realm of Vharn. When the border wards collapse and the stars go dark, she learns her late mother was a covenant-keeper—and that Lior's own memory has been edited to hide it. Hunted by guild assassins and guided by a shapeshifting exile called the Wolf, she must gather three scattered covenant-stones and reforge the pact at the Nightless Altar before the realms tear apart. In the end, Lior sacrifices her own memories of her found family to seal the covenant, only to discover that love, like ledgers, can be rewritten back.
about_author: Kestrel Thornbury is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obscure grimoires before turning to fiction. They live near a fog-bound coastline and write stories about people who inherit burdens they never asked for.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Impossibilities
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She catalogs impossible goods—a jar of bottled thunder, a key that opens yesterday—while dodging questions about her past. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine masking deep loneliness.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The border wards fail; stars vanish one by one as guild masters panic. A wounded stranger collapses into the Ledgerhouse. Emotional beat: fear cracking open her carefully hidden life.

chapters.title: A Wolf at the Door
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The stranger, Fen, half-wolf and half-man, carries a shattered covenant-stone that resonates with Lior's blood. Emotional beat: reluctant recognition—she knows his scent from dreams she shouldn't have.

chapters.title: What the Guild Keeps Below
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. Descending into the Ledgerhouse vaults, he sees the guild hoarding covenant relics while pretending neutrality. Emotional beat: bitter disillusionment with human institutions.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Her ledger entries begin rewriting themselves, revealing gaps in her own memory. Emotional beat: vertigo of self-doubt—who edited her, and why?

chapters.title: The Master of Ledgers
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Guildmaster Corvane reveals her mother was a covenant-keeper, then orders her detained 'for her safety.' Emotional beat: betrayal dressed as protection.

chapters.title: Running on Borrowed Roads
chapters.summary: Lior and Fen escape through a smuggler's moon-path. POV alternates. Emotional beat: first fragile trust forged in flight.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. They find a town whose residents lost all memory when the wards fell. An old woman mistakes Lior for her daughter. Emotional beat: grief as warning of what Lior might lose.

chapters.title: Hollow Stars
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At an observatory ruin, they learn the stars are caged souls of old covenant-keepers—including, perhaps, her mother. Emotional beat: hope tangled with horror.

chapters.title: Corvane's Hounds
chapters.summary: Guild assassins attack; Fen is gravely wounded shielding Lior. Lior's POV. Emotional beat: guilt and the dawning truth that invisibility costs others dearly.

chapters.title: The Hedge-Witch's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Hidden in her mother's old cottage, a memory-charm unlocks: her mother chose to forget to protect her. Emotional beat: fury softening into understanding.

chapters.title: Salt and Ash
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. He confesses his exile: he broke the covenant once before, believing humans unworthy. Emotional beat: shame met with unexpected absolution.

chapters.title: The Market of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Both POVs. They trade memories for the second stone's location among traveling peddlers. Emotional beat: bittersweet barter—what is a self worth?

chapters.title: Two Stones, One Hand
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The stones fuse to her skin, flooding her with ancestral memories of the original pact. Emotional beat: inheritance as both gift and weight.

chapters.title: The Bridge of Teeth
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. Crossing into Vharn, they face the realm's feral border-guardians. Fen must claim his alpha birthright or die. Emotional beat: courage reclaimed from disgrace.

chapters.title: Court of the Long Winter
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The wolf-court blames humanity for the failing stars; Lior argues her case using ledger-craft, proving the guild's treachery. Emotional beat: the invisible girl finally seen.

chapters.title: Corvane Ascendant
chapters.summary: Corvane seizes the third stone and begins forging a new covenant with himself as sole keeper. Alternating POV. Emotional beat: dread—the enemy isn't chaos but control.

chapters.title: The Price of the Altar
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The Nightless Altar demands a keeper's dearest memories as payment. She says goodbye to Fen without telling him why. Emotional beat: quiet devastation.

chapters.title: Reforge the Covenant
chapters.summary: Climax. Lior and Fen battle Corvane atop the altar; she completes the rite as the stars reignite, losing every memory of her found family. Alternating POV. Emotional beat: triumph laced with terrible cost.

chapters.title: A Stranger's Kindness
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. Memory-less Lior wakes among wolves; Fen chooses patience over grief, retelling their story day by day. Emotional beat: tenderness without expectation.

chapters.title: Ledgers Can Be Rewritten
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Discovering her own handwriting in the covenant-ledger, she performs the counter-rite, buying her memories back with a lesser price—her guild invisibility forever. Emotional beat: choosing to be seen.

chapters.title: Jonah and the Wolf
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. Lior becomes the new covenant-keeper, Fen her equal partner; the guild reformed under honest hands. Under returned stars, they write a new first entry together. Emotional beat: home found, not inherited but built.
